title: Agents operations
description: The two validators, each a command-line script that reads a repository and reports whether its files are well-formed. Both only read.

entities.name: Validate views and actors
entities.description: Checks the nine view schemas and their fictional examples, then every .dev/*.json diagram and behavior view in the repository (skipping .git, node_modules, build output and the skills folder itself, and leaving knowledge kinds to validate_knowledge.py): schema, unique IDs, relationship endpoints, the folder it claims, cited sources, child diagrams, use-case alternatives and related views. If the repository has an Actors/ folder, every actor field, actorDocument and Markdown link to Actors/<name>.md must land on a file, and every actor file must be linked from another file.
entities.transport: Command line: python3 Agents/Skills/validate_diagrams.py [repository-root]; in an adopting repository, python3 Meta/Agents/Skills/validate_diagrams.py. Without an argument the root is three folders above the script (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]).
entities.authorization: Nothing checks; anyone with a checkout and Python with jsonschema installed can run it.
entities.result: One line counting the schemas and examples validated, the views of each kind and the actor files, and exit status 0.
failures: The first problem found stops the run with a ValueError naming the file and the problem, and a non-zero exit status.
No diagrams found, when the repository has no view at all.
Run here without an argument, the root is the folder that contains this repository, not the repository (see the backlog item validate-diagrams-default-root).
ModuleNotFoundError when jsonschema is not installed.

entities.name: Validate knowledge files
entities.description: Checks every knowledge schema and that each kind has a fictional example that validates, then every .dev/*.json file whose kind is in the catalogue (skipping .git, node_modules and build output): its schema, that it is named after its kind, its $schema and folder, unique entity IDs, and that every path and entityId it mentions exists. Files of other kinds are skipped.
entities.transport: Command line: python3 Agents/Knowledge/validate_knowledge.py [repository-root]; in an adopting repository, python3 Meta/Agents/Knowledge/validate_knowledge.py. Without an argument the root is the current directory.
entities.authorization: Nothing checks; anyone with a checkout and Python with jsonschema installed can run it.
entities.result: Each problem as a line naming the file, then a line counting the kinds, examples, knowledge files checked and problems; exit status 0 when there are none.
failures: Exit status 1 when any example or knowledge file has a problem; every problem is listed, not only the first.
A kind without an example is reported as Missing example.
ModuleNotFoundError when jsonschema is not installed.

relatedViews.relationship: The use case whose steps run them.
